title: Odd and even numbers
examples: Teacher, what makes a number even?
If I have 9 fingers, is that odd or even?
Can you show me a pair of things?

explain.say: Look at these two apples. We can make one perfect pair.
When we have two things, they always make a pair. This means the number is even.

draw.text: Two things make a pair. Number is even.

explain.say: Now look at these three balloons. We can make one pair, but one is left over.
If one thing is left over, the number is odd. It does not make a perfect pair.

draw.text: Left over = Odd. Perfect pair = Even.

explain.say: For our real life example, think about socks. If you have four socks, you get two perfect pairs.
A common mistake is thinking that all big numbers are even. Remember to always check for a leftover.

items: Count the objects in groups of two.
If nothing is left, it is even.
If one is left, it is odd.

draw.text: Check for leftovers. Is it even or odd?

faq.q: What is the difference between odd and even numbers?
faq.a: Even numbers can always be split into perfect pairs with nothing left over. Odd numbers always have one item left over after making pairs.
asks: How do I know if a number is even?
Can you explain odd versus even?

faq.q: Does the number zero count as even or odd?
faq.a: Zero is considered an even number because you can make zero pairs with nothing left over. It is the starting point for counting pairs.
asks: What is the rule for zero?

faq.q: If I count up to ten, how many pairs do I have?
faq.a: When you count to ten, you have five perfect pairs. Ten is an even number because it divides exactly by two.

faq.q: Do I have to use objects to know if a number is odd?
faq.a: No, you can look at the number itself. If the number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9, it is odd. If it ends in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8, it is even.
asks: What do the last digits tell me?
Is there a trick for big numbers?

faq.q: What about numbers like eleven or nineteen?
faq.a: Eleven is odd because after making five pairs, one item remains. Nineteen is also odd because one item will be left over.

facts: Even numbers can always be divided exactly by two.
Odd numbers always have a remainder of one when divided by two.
The number zero is an even number.
All numbers ending in 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8 are even.

quiz.say: If you have nine crayons, what will be left over?
quiz.why: Nine crayons make four pairs with one crayon left over.

wrong.1: Zero means every single crayon was paired up perfectly.
wrong.2: Two would mean you made an extra pair.
wrong.3: Three is too many to be the leftover amount.

quiz.why: Twelve can be split into six perfect pairs of two.

wrong.0: Eleven is odd because it has a leftover piece.
wrong.2: Thirteen has one item left over after making pairs.
wrong.3: Fifteen always leaves one item remaining.
